title: Sediment sampling with a core sampler equipped with aluminum tubes and an onboard processing protocol to avoid plastic contamination
author: Tsuchiya, Nomaki, et al.

steps.title: Fabricate aluminum sampling tubes
steps.instruction: Obtain aluminum tubes matching conventional corer dimensions: outer diameter 89 mm. For a push corer use inner diameter 82 mm and length 320 mm; for a multiple corer use inner diameter 74 mm or 82 mm and length 600 mm. Ensure only the push‑core inner diameter is modified as needed.

steps.title: Install tubes on coring device
steps.instruction: Secure the appropriate aluminum tube onto the push corer or multiple corer, confirming a tight fit identical to that of standard polycarbonate or acrylic tubes.

steps.title: Deploy corer and collect sediment
steps.instruction: Lower the equipped corer to the seafloor, record the sampling coordinates (e.g., 35°0.9540′ N, 139°13.3250′ E) and depth (e.g., 855 m), then retrieve the core while keeping the aluminum tube sealed to avoid external contamination.

steps.title: Extrude core with aluminum head
steps.instruction: Use a core extruder whose contacting head is made of aluminum (not PVC) to extrude the sediment core without damaging the tube wall.

steps.title: Slice core using metal plate
steps.instruction: Place the extruded core on a metal cutting plate and slice the sediment into the desired layers, preserving the vertical integrity of each interval.
